standard.title: Automotive Vehicles — Noise Emitted by Moving Vehicles — Specification and Method of Measurement
standard.sector: Transport Engineering / Automotive Braking Systems, Vehicle Testing, Steering and Performance Evaluation

sectional_committee.name: Automotive Braking Systems, Vehicle Testing and Performance Evaluation Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard specifies the requirements and test evaluation methods for determining the external noise emitted by road vehicles in moving condition (pass-by noise). It is structured in multiple parts based on vehicle classification: Part 1 specifies limits and measurement methods for L2 category two-wheelers; Part 2 specifies limits and methods for categories other than L2 and L5 (covering M and N passenger and commercial road vehicles); and Part 3 specifies limits and methods for L5 (three-wheelers), L7 (quadricycles), E-rickshaws, and E-carts. It establishes mandatory acoustic limits at the manufacturing stage to control environmental noise pollution.

amendments.summary: Aligns two-wheeler noise measurement procedures with modern ECE standards.
Refines acceleration and calculation procedures for high-power passenger vehicles.

Overhauls standard title and scope to formally cover L5, L7, E-rickshaw, and E-cart categories under moving conditions; establishes Table 1A and Table 1B to regulate specific decibel thresholds for thermic and battery-operated three-wheelers.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under Rule 120 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR), 1989, all road-going vehicles manufactured or registered in India must undergo mandatory pass-by noise type-approval (homologation) testing. Compliance with IS 3028 noise limits must be certified by designated government testing agencies (such as ARAI, GARC, or ICAT) prior to commercial vehicle release. Non-conforming vehicles cannot be registered or legally operated on Indian public roads. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to acoustic emission parameters.
requirements: Requires a standardized open-air testing pad comprising an acceleration track and a centralized measurement zone. Two microphones must be positioned symmetrically on both sides of the vehicle's driving centerline at a distance of 7.5 m ± 0.05 m from the path axis and at a height of 1.2 m ± 0.02 m above the track surface.

The test track pavement must satisfy strict ISO 10844 acoustic criteria. Pavement residual void content is limited to <= 8%, and the surface sound absorption coefficient must not exceed 0.10. Additionally, the macrotexture depth must be greater than or equal to 0.4 mm to prevent tire rolling-noise absorption or scattering.

Acoustic measurements are sensitive to atmospheric parameters. Outdoor wind speed at microphone height must not exceed 5 m/s during test intervals to prevent wind-induced microphone distortion. Background environmental ambient noise must be at least 10 dB(A) lower than the vehicle's peak emitted sound level.

The test evaluates sound levels under worst-case acceleration. The vehicle must approach the test line at a specified speed (or engine RPM) in a selected gear, and then accelerate at wide-open-throttle (WOT) until the rear of the vehicle exits the test zone. The peak sound level recorded on the sound level meter (A-weighted, fast response) is taken as the evaluation result.

Under Part 2 modern norms (aligned with ECE R51.03), maximum limits for passenger cars are set between 72 dB(A) to 75 dB(A), while heavy commercial vehicles (N3 category) are restricted based on engine power ranges (varying from 80 dB(A) to 85 dB(A) depending on engine output and GVW limits).

At least four measurements must be conducted on each side of the vehicle for each gear configuration. The test results are considered valid only if the difference between consecutive runs on the same side does not exceed 2 dB(A). The highest mean value calculated from the loudest side constitutes the official sound level.
